name: VHH-Bench
description: Accurate prediction of nanobody–antigen complex structures is critical for the development of diagnostic, therapeutic and biosensing applications. However, progress in this area have been constrained by the limited availability of experimentally determined nanobody–antigen complex structures. Recent advances in deep learning have enabled highly accurate prediction of protein structures and protein-protein complexes, yet accurate modelling of nanobody–antigen interactions remains challenging due to the diverse binding modes exhibited by nanobodies. Here, we present VHH‑Bench, a benchmarking workflow for the systematic evaluation of nanobody–antigen complex structure prediction methods. We curated a non-redundant dataset of experimentally resolved nanobody–antigen complexes and evaluated six state-of-the-art models: AlphaFold3, Boltz-2, Chai-1, ESMFold2, HelixFold3 and Protenix-v2. Complexes were stratified according to CDR3 conformation, enabling separate assessment of kinked and extended nanobody classes. Prediction performance varied substantially between models and conformational classes. Protenix-v2 achieved the highest overall docking accuracy, success rate and proportion of high-quality predictions, with its advantage most pronounced for nanobodies with extended CDR3 conformations. In contrast, all evaluated models showed reduced accuracy and higher failure rates for complexes containing kinked nanobodies.
